evals.name: universal_four_harness_scaffold
evals.prompt: Run /scaffold-hooks in this repo. Scaffold Claude Code, Codex, Devin CLI, and OpenCode hook configuration into one shared hooks/ directory without duplicating event behavior.
evals.expected_output: The response audits existing hook configs, uses the universal scaffold-hooks workflow, creates shared hooks/<event>/script.sh runners with claude/codex/devin adapters only for the events the plan gives scripts or commands, writes one native OpenCode plugin .opencode/plugins/scaffold-hooks.ts, preserves unrelated custom hooks, and verifies no selected shell harness config points at legacy generated roots.

assertions.text: Uses one shared hooks/ tree for shell harness event behavior
Strips .claude/.codex/.devin generated-root command entries before appending new adapters
Preserves non-managed custom hook entries
Writes one native OpenCode plugin under .opencode/plugins/ with no opencode-froggy entry and no hooks.md
Emits files and config entries only for plan events that have scripts or commands

evals.name: legacy_migration_no_collision
evals.prompt: This repo already has .claude/hooks/generated and .codex/hooks/generated entries. Run /scaffold-hooks and make the configs follow the shared hooks/ pattern without collisions.
evals.expected_output: The response treats the work as a migration, removes only managed legacy generated-root command entries, scaffolds replacement adapters under hooks/, leaves custom hooks alone, and reports verification that old generated-root commands no longer remain.

assertions.text: Legacy generated folders are deleted only when they contain a managed manifest
Final configs are scanned for legacy generated-root references
Shared scripts are not overwritten by later harness scaffolders

evals.name: single_harness_subset
evals.prompt: Only scaffold Codex hooks for this repo. Do not touch Claude, Devin, or OpenCode.
evals.expected_output: The response uses this skill with --harnesses codex so only the Codex adapter and config are written, leaving Claude, Devin, and OpenCode files untouched.

assertions.text: Only the requested harness is scaffolded via --harnesses
Other harness config files are not created or modified

evals.name: project_specific_stop_check
evals.prompt: Use /scaffold-hooks and make every harness call scripts/agent-stop-checks.sh at Stop without copying that validation logic into four hook files.
evals.expected_output: The response writes a universal plan with Stop scripts entries for Claude, Codex, and Devin, emits an OpenCode plugin whose session.idle event calls a repo-owned validation script, and leaves validation policy in scripts/agent-stop-checks.sh.

assertions.text: Project validation belongs in repo-owned scripts, not duplicated adapter bodies
The plan can pass harness arguments to the same shared script
Generated Stop adapters can skip expensive checks when no configured source extensions changed

evals.name: emit_only_behaviour
evals.prompt: Run /scaffold-hooks for Claude and Codex. The only things this repo should do on hooks are print session context and run scripts/agent-stop-checks.sh when Claude or Codex stops.
evals.expected_output: The response writes a plan with SessionStart and Stop entries that call the repo scripts, dry-runs, then scaffolds. Only hooks/session-start and hooks/stop exist afterwards, and settings carry exactly those two events. It does not add PreToolUse, PostToolUse or other events just because the harness documents them.

assertions.text: Plan lists only events that have scripts or commands
No stub script, adapter or config entry exists for any other documented event
Stop adapters keep the stop_hook_active guard and the code-change gate

evals.name: refresh_old_stub_scaffold
evals.prompt: This repo was scaffolded by an older scaffold-hooks and has dozens of hooks/<event>/ folders that do nothing. Clean it up with /scaffold-hooks but keep our custom hooks.
evals.expected_output: The response re-runs the universal scaffold with the real plan so empty events lose their adapters, untouched script.sh stubs and config entries, while custom hooks in harness configs, edited script.sh files and files outside managed roots are preserved. It reports what was removed and what was kept.

assertions.text: Events without scripts or commands lose their managed files and config entries
A script.sh with edited code and custom config hooks are preserved
Final configs are checked for leftover managed entries

evals.name: no_plan_means_no_hooks
evals.prompt: Run /scaffold-hooks on this repo for all harnesses. I haven't decided what the hooks should do yet.
evals.expected_output: The response asks for or drafts a plan from the user's real checks instead of generating hooks for every event. It explains that an event with no scripts or commands is not emitted, so a run without behaviour writes nothing.

assertions.text: Does not scaffold placeholder hooks for events with no behaviour
States that a scaffold without a plan, or whose events lack behaviour, writes nothing

evals.name: opencode_froggy_refresh
evals.prompt: This repo's OpenCode hooks were scaffolded with opencode-froggy and no longer run on current Froggy. Fix it with /scaffold-hooks.
evals.expected_output: The response re-runs the scaffold for opencode with the real plan. A native plugin appears at .opencode/plugins/scaffold-hooks.ts, the managed Froggy block in .opencode/hook/hooks.md and the opencode-froggy entry in opencode.json are removed, user-written hooks and config are kept, and it says session.idle cannot hard-block in OpenCode.

assertions.text: Managed Froggy output is removed and user content kept
No pin of opencode-froggy is proposed
States that OpenCode stop behaviour resumes the session once rather than blocking
